archetypes.name: sweep-completeness
archetypes.rationale: Plan defers Family B writer fence discovery to implementation time across 11+ files; undiscovered call sites would silently leave orphan risk in production.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the Markdown and skill files listed for the fence sweep are exhaustive: grep for each of the five top-level Family B writer basenames (ship-pr.sh, run-step5-review.sh, run-step2-dispatch.sh, collect-agent-results.sh, dispatch-plan-voters.sh) across the full repo tree including .claude/skills/, agents/, and any unlisted references/ directories. Compare actual grep hits against the plan's named file list and flag any call sites the plan did not enumerate. Also check whether per-file statements such as 'sweep collect-agent-results.sh fences if any' are backed by actual fence evidence in those files or are speculative no-ops that might cause the implementer to skip real sites. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: lint-regex-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The proposed lint helper's identifier-extraction logic must handle all named PID-capture and wait variants; a missed pattern silently re-introduces the orphan bug behind a green lint pass.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's proposed fence_has_family_b_pid_capture_and_wait helper specification for regex completeness: confirm it accepts all named PID-capture variants (VAR=$! with and without a leading local qualifier) and all three named wait forms (double-quoted, unquoted, and brace-quoted versions of the captured identifier). Check whether the four new fixture cases in test-lint-foreground-markers.sh cover the local-VAR=$! variant, the multi-fence look-ahead window where the wait appears in the fence after the writer anchor, and the identifier-mismatch failure mode described as Failure Mode 2 in the plan. Also verify that the plan's Failure Mode 1 mitigation ('at minimum warn on missing ampersand') is consistent with how the existing linter exits on violations, since a warn-not-fail path would not block CI and could silently permit the degraded streaming scenario the plan explicitly calls out. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: exit-code-discard
archetypes.rationale: The plan's wait with 2>/dev/null || true unconditionally drops the writer's exit code; if any orchestrator step branches on the wrapper task's exit status, ship-pr.sh failures would be silently swallowed.
archetypes.prompt_body: Determine whether any orchestrator or skill step reads the exit code of the wrapper Bash task that invokes a top-level Family B writer, specifically whether skills/implement/SKILL.md Step 8 branching logic inspects the task exit status to detect ship-pr.sh failure, since the proposed wait with 2>/dev/null || true would mask that signal. Also verify that the plan's claim about breadcrumb-monitor.sh SIGKILL escalation ('wait then returns within ~5 seconds') is consistent with the actual SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL sequence in the real breadcrumb-monitor.sh, and that adding wait does not extend the effective timeout beyond the monitor's 1800-second bound in the case where the writer itself hangs after the monitor's kill attempt. Finally check whether test-background-monitor-wait.sh validates the exit-code-discard behavior explicitly or only the timing invariant, leaving the silent-failure regression undetected. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
